Verify Polynomial Pools Matrix Properties

Source: R/pp_matrix.R
pp_verify.Rd

Check whether a matrix produced by pp_matrix has the expected PP dimensions, row sizes, and column weights, and print a concise validation summary.

Usage

pp_verify(M)

Arguments

M

A binary pooling matrix, typically returned by pp_matrix. If the "pp" attribute is present, its stored parameters are included in the printed summary.

Value

Invisibly returns a named list with:

n_pools

Integer; the row dimension \(J\)

n_samples

Integer; the column dimension \(N\)

pool_size

Integer; the first observed row sum \(n_j\)

sample_coverage

Integer; the first observed column sum \(w_i\)

uniform_pools

Logical; TRUE if all row sums are equal

uniform_coverage

Logical; TRUE if all column sums are equal

The function also prints a verification summary showing \(J\), \(N\), row sums, column sums, compression, and density.

Details

For a PP matrix \(\mathbf{M} \in \{0,1\}^{J \times N}\), the key structural quantities are $$n_j = |\mathcal{P}_j| = \sum_{i=1}^N M_{ji}$$ and $$w_i = |\mathcal{J}_i| = \sum_{j=1}^J M_{ji}.$$ In the untruncated PP design, every row sum is \(q^{d-1}\) and every column sum is \(n_l\). When \(N < q^d\), truncation preserves the common column weight \(w_i = n_l\) but may disturb row uniformity near the truncation boundary. This function reports whether the realized row and column sums are uniform, along with the empirical compression ratio $$\frac{N}{J}.$$

Relationship to pp_matrix and pp_design

  • pp_design: Planning - find valid configurations

  • pp_matrix: Construction - generate the matrix

  • pp_verify: Validation - check the result

Properties Checked

  1. Uniform pool sizes: All pools contain the same number of samples

  2. Uniform sample coverage: All samples appear in the same number of pools

  3. Correct dimensions: \(M = n_l \times q\) pools, \(N \leq q^d\) samples

  4. Stored parameters match: q, d, nl, k_max

References

Tan, Y. H. I. (2020). Pooling matrix designs for group testing. SIAM Undergraduate Research Online, 13, 1-21.

Brust, D., & Brust, J. J. (2023). Effective matrix designs for COVID-19 group testing. BMC Bioinformatics, 24, Article 26.

See also

pp_matrix, pp_design, pp_decode

Other polynomial_pools: polynomial_pools, pp_design(), pp_matrix()

Examples

# Generate and verify P-BEST matrix
M <- pp_matrix(q = 8, d = 3, nl = 6, N = 384)
result <- pp_verify(M)
#> 
#> === PP Matrix Verification ===
#> Dimensions: 48 pools x 384 samples
#> Parameters: q = 8, d = 3, nl = 6
#> Detection limit: k_max = 2
#> Expected pool size: 48
#> 
#> Structure:
#>   Pool sizes: 48 (uniform yes)
#>   Pools/sample: 6 (uniform yes)
#>   Compression: 8x
#>   Matrix density: 0.125
result
#> $n_pools
#> [1] 48
#> 
#> $n_samples
#> [1] 384
#> 
#> $pool_size
#> [1] 48
#> 
#> $sample_coverage
#> [1] 6
#> 
#> $uniform_pools
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $uniform_coverage
#> [1] TRUE
#> 

# Access verification results
result$pool_size      # 48 (note: depends on truncation)
#> [1] 48
result$uniform_pools  # TRUE
#> [1] TRUE

# Verify different designs
